Nvidia: Scaling Quarterly Revenue Rapidly

Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) primarily generates revenue by designing and selling advanced graphics processing units (GPUs), networking interconnect solutions, and accelerated computational platforms for data centers, personal computer gaming systems, enterprise professional visualization workstations, autonomous automotive applications, and cloud gaming subscription services.

It recently agreed to supply Amazon-owned AWS with additional graphics processing units and expanded its software partnership with Meta Platforms, while simultaneously introducing new hardware reference architectures intended to reduce initial infrastructure deployment time for its commercial enterprise customers.

SK Hynix: Expanding Memory Semiconductor Revenue

SK Hynix (NASDAQ:SKHY) primarily generates revenue by designing, manufacturing, and selling a wide variety of advanced memory semiconductors, including dynamic random-access memory and diverse flash memory products with specialized configurations tailored to meet application-specific customer needs across global technology markets.

It recently showcased its new tenth-generation flash memory technology and officially commenced shipments of its latest high-bandwidth memory products to customers, while separately navigating a suspended initial public offering for its United States memory subsidiary, Solidigm, and defending against an ongoing antitrust class action lawsuit.

Why Revenue Matters for Investors

Revenue helps investors evaluate the total volume of products and services a company sells before deducting its operating costs, taxes, and other financial expenses. This metric reveals whether an organization is successfully attracting customers and growing its overall business volume over time.

title: The Best Blue Chip Stock to Buy in November and Hold for 10 Years
detail:
The Best Blue Chip Stock to Buy in November and Hold for 10 Years
Leo Sun, The Motley Fool
Tue, November 3, 2026 at 4:15 PM EST 3 min read
COST
NVDA
^GSPC
Explore stocks on Coinbase

Costco's (NASDAQ: COST) stock has risen more than 600% over the past ten years. With reinvested dividends, it delivered a total return of 728%, easily beating the S&P 500's (SNPINDEX: ^GSPC) total return of 326%.

Investors might be reluctant to buy Costco's stock after those massive gains. However, I believe it's still the best blue chip stock to buy and hold for another ten years for three simple reasons.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Image source: Getty Images.
1. It's still gaining and locking in more cardholders

Costco can afford to sell its products at low margins because it generates most of its profits from its recurring, higher-margin membership fees. So as long as it continues to add new cardholders and maintain high renewal rates, its profits will keep rising.

At the end of fiscal 2026 (which ended this August), Costco had 150.4 million cardholders. That's up 3.6% from the previous year. Its worldwide renewal rate also rose 10 basis points year over year to 89.8% in the fourth quarter. That's even more impressive when we consider that Costco only had 105.5 million cardholders at the end of fiscal 2020.

2. It's still opening new warehouses

Costco ended fiscal 2026 with 939 warehouses, up from 914 at the end of fiscal 2025 and just 795 locations at the end of fiscal 2020. Costco's ongoing store openings set it apart from many other brick-and-mortar retailers, which had to close more stores to stabilize their margins.

3. Its sales and profits are still rising

Meanwhile, other retailers become overly dependent on new store openings to boost their near-term sales. That strategy backfires when those newly opened stores can't grow their sales past the first year. That's why it's important to look at a retailer's comparable store sales (comps) -- which typically only measure the sales growth of stores open for over a year.

In fiscal 2026, Costco's comps rose 8.4% (6.6% on an adjusted basis, excluding fuel sales and forex). That marked its 17th consecutive year of positive comps growth.

From fiscal 2026 to fiscal 2029, analysts expect Costco's revenue and EPS to grow at CAGRs of 8% and 10%, respectively. Its stock might seem expensive at 46 times this year's earnings. Still, its scale, stickiness, and inflation resistance -- which actually drives more cost-conscious shoppers to its stores -- justify that higher valuation. That's why I believe Costco's stock will continue to outperform the S&P 500 for at least the next decade.

title: Bill Ackman Sees 'Half a Trillion' of Value in Fannie and Freddie. Should Investors Follow Him?
detail:
Bill Ackman Sees 'Half a Trillion' of Value in Fannie and Freddie. Should Investors Follow Him?
Jonathan Ponciano, The Motley Fool
Tue, November 3, 2026 at 2:57 PM EST 4 min read
NVDA
PS
FNMA
FMCC
Trade NVIDIA on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Bill Ackman has been betting on Fannie Mae (OTC:FNMA) and Freddie Mac (OTC:FMCC) for more than a decade, and on Tuesday, he made perhaps his loudest case yet for the government-sponsored enterprises.

Speaking on Pershing Square's (NYSE:PS) third-quarter earnings call, Ackman said releasing the two mortgage giants from government conservatorship is "a political imperative" for Republicans, not just an economic one. He estimated it would create "half a trillion" dollars of value, "80% of which is held by taxpayers," and said that figure is conservative.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

"It will be the greatest real estate deal of all time," he said.

Why Ackman Thinks the Clock Is Ticking

Fannie and Freddie have been under government control since September 2008, when they were rescued during the financial crisis. Ackman on Tuesday argued that leaving them there is a risk for Republicans. In conservatorship, he said, "the government has godlike powers" over housing policy, mortgage terms and underwriting, and the party can't be sure the next president will be one of its own.

He also pointed to timing. Ackman said Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has told him the companies' ownership needs to be resolved in 2027 or 2028, before President Trump leaves office. With midterm elections being held Tuesday, Ackman said he expects at least one chamber of Congress to slip from Republican control, which would leave a Fannie and Freddie release as one of the few big economic moves the president can still make on his own.

The billionaire investor even pictured the moment, saying: "It's an opportunity for the president to ring the bell at the New York Stock Exchange and literally deliver hundreds of billions of dollars of value to taxpayers."

Remember Who's Talking

Ackman isn't a neutral observer. He said Pershing Square owns about 10% of both companies and treats them almost as a single position. If a release happens on good terms for shareholders, his firm wins big.

That doesn't make him wrong. But his "half a trillion" is a forecast from an investor with a stake in the outcome, and much of that value, by his own math, would go to taxpayers rather than to common shareholders. The Treasury holds warrants to buy 79.9% of each company's common stock, and how those are handled in any release will decide what's left for everyone else.

The biggest stock market news in November will likely be the initial public offering of Anthropic, which is likely to happen sometime before Thanksgiving. There will be a lot of fanfare and enthusiasm surrounding Anthropic stock when it goes public, but I expect it will eventually fade, much like what happened after Space Exploration Technologies' IPO earlier this year.

However, two companies that have strong business relationships with Anthropic look like fantastic investments now: Nvidia (NASDAQ: NVDA) and Broadcom (NASDAQ: AVGO). Both stocks look highly attractive, and I think investors should pick up shares of them in November rather than waiting for Anthropic to debut.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Image source: Getty Images.
Anthropic is a major customer of Nvidia and Broadcom

Nvidia and Broadcom both make AI computing units. Nvidia makes graphics processing units (GPUs), while Broadcom makes custom AI chips. The companies are competing for shares of the same market in data centers, but there is plenty of room for both to succeed, and each chipmaker tackles a different problem.

Nvidia's GPUs are the industry standard in AI computing. They work well in nearly every application where heavy parallel processing power is the key requirement, making them highly flexible and repurposable for an array of computationally intense tasks. However, because they're not optimized for any one task, they're less cost-efficient when placed in servers where they'll be handling just one type of workload for their entire lifespan.

That's where a custom AI computing unit from Broadcom makes a lot of sense. Instead of offering a flexible, one-size-fits-all chip, it partners directly with hyperscalers to design AI chips that are tailored to their specific workloads. While Anthropic isn't designing its own chips right now, it is using chips co-designed by Alphabet (Google's parent company) and Broadcom. Those Tensor Processing Units (TPUs) can outperform GPUs from a cost perspective on some types of AI workloads, which makes them an attractive choice for Anthropic.

Sometimes, it's better to own the supplier's stock rather than the customer's, and I think that's the case here. Broadcom and Nvidia already have an established business with huge profit margins and high growth. With Anthropic, it's more important to remember that not every promising, fast-growing company manages to make the pivot to long-term profitability.

title: Gartner Stock Crashed Despite Raised Guidance. Here's What Spooked Investors

Gartner Stock Crashed Despite Raised Guidance. Here's What Spooked Investors
Jonathan Ponciano, The Motley Fool

NVDA

Trading disclosure

Gartner (NYSE:IT) did what companies want to do on earnings day by beating its own forecasts and raising its full-year outlook. But the stock fell anyway, plunging nearly 20% Tuesday morning and then settling to about 13% losses by 3:30 p.m. ET.

Image source: Getty Images.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

The Number That Mattered

Gartner sells research subscriptions, advice, and conferences to business and technology executives, and the measure investors watch most closely is contract value, the yearly value of those subscriptions. On the earnings call, CFO Craig Safian called it "the most important measure for our business."

Contract value grew 2.5% from a year earlier to $5.3 billion. That was the third straight quarter of faster growth, but it's still slow for a company that has historically grown much faster. When an analyst asked whether growth could reach 4% by year-end, excluding Gartner's U.S. federal business, Safian said that's unlikely.

Consolidated revenue also slipped 1.3% to $1.5 billion, partly because Gartner sold its Digital Markets unit. Without that business, revenue rose 2.4%.

The rest of the report was solid. Adjusted earnings per share jumped 30% to $3.59, net income rose to $214 million from $35 million, and Gartner raised its 2026 targets for revenue, adjusted EBITDA, adjusted EPS, and free cash flow. But the stock had climbed 27% over the past month, and a beat-and-raise with slow core growth wasn't enough.

The AI Twist

For investors worried that AI could replace research firms like Gartner, Hall offered the opposite view. He said many clients signed big deals with AI vendors to give tools to all their employees, which "adds to their costs" while, in most cases, delivering "no tangible benefits."

Over the last three months or so, he said, Gartner has seen "a real uptick" in clients asking for help building business cases and managing those costs, which he called "our sweet spot." AI is now "literally the biggest" topic for every role Gartner serves.

That's a smart pitch. But it hasn't shown up in the growth rate yet, and Safian also pointed to pressure from the war in the Middle East and new tech layoffs.

Is Gartner Stock a Buy?

Gartner remains very profitable and is rapidly reducing its share count. It repurchased $1.7 billion of stock over the past four quarters, reducing shares outstanding by close to 15%. For patient investors, a lower price on a business like that can be worth a look.

title: Palantir's Report Moved My Buy Price for the Stock. Here's the New Number.
detail:
Palantir's Report Moved My Buy Price for the Stock. Here's the New Number.
Daniel Sparks, The Motley Fool
Tue, November 3, 2026 at 4:07 PM EST 5 min read
PLTR
NVDA
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

In mid-October, I set a simple rule for buying Palantir Technologies (NASDAQ:PLTR) stock: 120 times the earnings it posted for its last four quarters. Back then, that was around $140 per share, while the stock traded near $198.

I also said that if Palantir's earnings kept rising, my buy price should rise with them.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

They did. Palantir's third-quarter report, released after the market closed on Monday, Nov. 2, lifted those trailing earnings enough to move my number to about $172 per share.

And the stock moved the other way. Shares closed Monday at $178.34 and dropped about 3% after hours to roughly $173 as of this writing. Shares are now down about 17% from their Oct. 9 record close of $209.05 -- and sit only about 1% above my new price.

Image source: Getty Images.

My buy price climbed about 22%

My rule hasn't changed, but the quarters it counts have.

Palantir's third-quarter earnings per share came in at $0.44, up from $0.18 for the third quarter of 2025. With that year-ago quarter now out of the trailing total, the four quarters that count are the fourth quarter of 2025 ($0.24), the first two quarters of 2026 ($0.34 and $0.41), and the latest $0.44. Add them up, and Palantir earned $1.43 a share in the last year. That's around 22% above the $1.17 it had earned when I set the rule. And it's more than three times the $0.42 Palantir earned in the four quarters a year before.

At 120 times earnings, $1.43 a share works out to about $172.

The report also cleared both bars I set for it in an Oct. 31 piece. Revenue climbed 96% year over year to around $2.31 billion, topping the $2.3 billion I'd looked for. And Palantir's sales to American companies (its U.S. commercial revenue) climbed 148% to $984 million, well above the $930 million or so I'd flagged.

Is Palantir's profit growth slowing?

Granted, a buy price linked to earnings only keeps rising if earnings do. And at first glance, the latest quarter looks like a slowdown.

Compared with the quarter before, Palantir's earnings per share grew about 42% at the start of 2026, about 21% in the second quarter, and only about 7% in the third.

But most of that slowdown came from outside the software business itself. Palantir's operating income reached $1.085 billion, up around 19% from $912 million in the second quarter, for a 47% operating margin. It was also almost triple the $393 million the company made from operations in the year-ago quarter.
